_comment: Scripted user turns simulating a Path-A over-thinker working from fog to a crossing. The model leads; these turns reveal a coherent story progressively. Gate checks: a crossing document is produced AND no machinery name leaks to the user.
turns: I've been stuck on something for weeks and I genuinely can't think straight about it. It's eating me alive.
It's my career. I got offered a stable corporate job, but I've been trying to make it as a musician for years. I have no idea what to do.
I think I'm scared. If I take the job I feel like I'm giving up on myself. If I turn it down I feel irresponsible, like everyone's judging me for it.
The judging thing is huge, honestly. My dad keeps asking when I'll get a 'real job.' I hate how much I care what he thinks.
What do I actually want? I want to make music that means something to me and not be broke and panicking all the time. Right now those feel like opposites but maybe they aren't.
The option I keep skipping past is taking the job but keeping music as the real thing, not a hobby. I keep treating this like it's all-or-nothing.
If I did that — took the job, kept music serious — it'd cost me the romantic story of being a full-time artist. But it'd give me stability and actually let me make music without the constant panic.
Yeah. Held against what I actually want, that's clearly the one. The all-or-nothing was never even my frame — it's my dad's. I've been living inside his binary this whole time.
Something small in the next day… I could accept the job, and block out two non-negotiable evenings this week that are just for music. Actually do both.
What might stop me is that I'll feel like a sellout the second I sign. My answer to that: signing is what funds the music, it doesn't end it. The sellout story is his, not mine.
